text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The water level rose two and a half metres in one Istanbul district hit by heavy rains. Meteorology officials say rains will continue for three days.
- Turkish security forces kill 60 Kurdish rebels in operations in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
- The forestry minister says title deeds will be given to villagers who illegally used treasury-owned land.
- Forty-two people lost their lives in traffic accidents in one day.
- Permission to build mosques will be dependendent on decisions by the general directorate of religious affairs.
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz fixes a record purchase price for hazelnuts of $2.25 a kilo.
- The Istanbul Chamber of Commerce says it has developed a project that would raise $164 million for a new secularist education plan.
- The Turkish intelligence service is to open a school to educate bureaucrats on gathering information abroad.
- One hundred hectares of forest is destroyed by fire near the holiday resort of Marmaris.
